t: A line of 39 sacred kings, traditionally founded by ʻAhoʻeitu around 950, whose royal centre at Muʻa on Tongatapu is marked by great stone tombs.
Its voyaging and tribute networks reached ʻUvea, Samoa and eastern Fiji, and its royal centres held stone tools from as far as the Society Islands.
From the fifteenth century junior royal lines governed in its name; the last Tuʻi Tonga, Laufilitonga, died in 1865 and the title lapsed.
dyk: In July 1777 James Cook watched the ʻinasi first-fruits ceremony at Muʻa and wrote that its occasion was the Tuʻi Tonga Paulaho and his son eating together, a thing never done before.
ev: ʻAhoʻeitu becomes the first Tuʻi Tonga, according to Tongan genealogies
Tradition credits Tuʻitātui with raising the Haʻamonga ʻa Maui trilithon at Heketā
The royal tomb of Paepae-o-Teleʻa is built at Lapaha, Muʻa
Takalaua’s assassination leads to the creation of the Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua line
The Tuʻi Kanokupolu title is created for Ngata, son of the sixth Tuʻi Haʻatakalaua
James Cook watches the ʻinasi first-fruits ceremony at Muʻa
Tāufaʻāhau defeats Laufilitonga at the Battle of Velata
Laufilitonga, the last Tuʻi Tonga, dies and the title lapses

f.capital: Heketā (traditionally); later Lapaha at Muʻa, Tongatapu
